reviews.text: Look at the big dawg, watching Green Book in 2026. I guess I’m a masochist. It steps on every rake imaginable when it comes to any kind of greater(or lesser) commentary, but it’s an extremely easy watch. Mahershala Ali continues to prove that he may very well be the greatest actor since the 2010s began, and maybe of the 21st century(despite having precious little to work with).

Doc Shirley goes on tour with a man whose never seen racism before, written as such so he can guffaw at every bit of discrimination. Shirley also is written to have no survival instinct it seems, just so he can teach him about sundown towns and segregation. I found the movie to be a well-shot, well-acted (given the script), but overwhelmingly milquetoast commentary on Jim Crow America. Maybe I'm judging it based on its critical success more than it as a movie alone but as a Best Picture(!) and Best Original Screenplay (insane) winner, I thought it fell flat.

I can’t say I didn’t enjoy the watch it was charming BUT reading the articles/interviews about Shirley’s family disapproving it and their reasoning and also having no say in it really made this hard to love

2.5 stars given because there were some nice shots and the "based off a true story" is kinda neat. I withheld a good rating however because of how truly predictable it was. The movie wasn't solely about the racism in the south, it was a Trojan horse for a plethora of liberal ideologies grouped under the main race related issue. The black dude was caught having gay sex in the YMCA and that's supposed to just be accepted. This review was written in a bathroom stall which I think is appropriate for this film.

O resultado é só um filme de Natal fofinho mesmo, e eu amo Buddy trips, então deu pra aproveitar a experiência…
Got worse the more I thought about it. The most interesting character and subject in the movie was sidelined for the main white guy to look like one of the good ones
favorite scene is the one where tony gets shirley out of trouble at the ymca and is like "don'worry dahc i'm from da bronx, i noo th'world had gays init"

Lembro que gostei muito da primeira vez que assisti, depois começei a pensar na questão de ser um filme meio problematico principalmente pela maneira como aborda o relacionamento entre tony e don, ainda acho um filme divertido, funciona bem pra passar o tempo e dar umas risadas mas tinha potencial pra ser um filme muito melhor.

BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO Bad. Boring. If this movie was trying to make a point about discrimination, what a wildly off the mark attempt. And for these interactions with racism to be what drives so many of the plot points and still not able to make a salient point is truly wild. Mahershala Ali is a great actor but this is not a good performance. He is insanely robotic and hard to appreciate. While Viggo Mortensen's character had some actually funny moments, I thought they leaned to heavy into the Italian angle of his background.

watching this for class and i cant lie its rlly not as bad as ppl say. its def a corny race movie and its wild that it was made in 2018 but i wouldn't call it a black trauma movie or a white savior movie rlly just….corny or maybe surface level. music wise, great shit

Not as bad as I feared, but not good either. A cartoon of racial reconciliation,  with some fun performances. Schmaltzy, simple, self-congratulatory, kinda dull. People made fun of how broad Viggo goes, but broad is is the order of the day. He made me laugh. 🤷‍♂️

Not enough Linda Cardellini. Never enough Linda Cardellini. The worst thing that ever happened to this film was winning Best Picture. It would not have deserved to be recognized as the best picture any year since 1905 but it's not a bad movie. When it's not being oblivious, it's extremely average. What Chasing Amy was to queer issues, Green Book is to racial issues. (Not a compliment.) Before I dunk on this film, both Ali and Mortensen are doing great work. Almost worth a watch on the merit of that alone. It's entertaining in the way that unlikely animal friend videos on the internet are. For a movie about musicians they picked a lot of crappy songs for the soundtrack. There was plenty that didn't sound right to me about this film. Besides the music, I never 100% bought Mortensen's accent, either. I can't deny some genuine poignant moments but unless you're specifically seeking the cinematic equivalent of muzak, best to avoid Green Book.

Nice wholesome, easy to enjoy and heartwarming movie. It would be completely forgettable and cheesy, guilty of being a 1990's movie made in 2018, if it werent a true story. Also saved by the acting of Vigo and Mahershala. There's just something infallible with stories about people who are opposite, little in common, who end up overcoming their difference to build a complementary relationship.
I’ve seen clips of this on TikTok for years so thought I should finally give it a go. Seems quite safe and watered down for the themes it presents. But the acting, music and visuals I enjoyed.

Idk I thought this was kind of a cute little buddy road trip film with some great performances at the top of the cast list. The racial themes leave a lot to be desired and I really don’t understand how it is so critically acclaimed with such surface level thematic elements but whatever, I never understand the academy anyway.

most of this was pretty middling until that bar/club scene right towards the end where you get to see the film portray true musical genius. The back to back classical to jazz sequence is such a fun bit it kinda makes up for the rest of the suffering you have to do in the other parts of the film. Not bad, not great, but not bad!

Me pareció una película la vrd muy realista a lo que era la perspectiva de las personas negras en esa época, me gustó que no mostraban a Tony como el “blanco único que ve a los negro como igual” si no que se ve como al principio el igual tenía su prejuicio y desprecio hacia las otras etnias, en el transcurso de la película vemos las dificultades del Dr. en todos los lugares desde donde dormir hasta donde simplemente comer. Lo cual es súper estúpido porq como lo van a llamar para tocar y no dejarlo ni comer en el propio lugar es muy contradictorio y solo muestra lo descarado que eran en esos tiempos.

Thoroughly watchable film in the clap-to-end-racism genre. Newcastle University are going to put up a statue of Tony Lip hugging Don Shirley as they both stand victoriously on top of a dying carcass wearing a hat with the word “prejudice” written on it.

Man, we don’t make neoliberal films like how we used to. Take me back to the late 2010s, when every self-respecting establishment director was set on making a “mark👏the👏vans👏” flick. We poke fun, but where’s our Green Book now?

don shirley’s family were completely left out of this film and felt there were false narratives sooooo it’s does feel weird now. but! i enjoyed while i watched and i loved Mahershala Ali‘s performance

Olha... é um bom filme, mas nada genial. Entrei esperando algo bem mais chato e, no fim, foi uma experiência bem ok; até melhor do que eu esperava. Os diálogos funcionam, para mim o filme não é cansativo e a dinâmica entre os personagens é muito boa. O Tony Lip é um personagem carismático e a atuação do Mahershala Ali, que faz o Don, é excelente e, em vários momentos, é o que mais eleva o filme. Ao mesmo tempo, achei que o filme é bastante convencional e não acho que aprofunde tanto os temas que aborda. É uma história fácil de acompanhar, agradável e pode ser até emocional, mas que dificilmente chega a ser memorável. No geral, ok. Foi uma surpresa mais positiva que negativa, principalmente porque minhas expectativas eram baixíssimas.

Nunca se gana con la violencia. Solo se gana cuando mantienes la dignidad. Esta interesante, al ser una historia real me llama más la atención la forma en la que se genera la amistad entre ambos protagonistas. Más allá no tengo algo que destacar. Es una critica social y me gusta como Shirley rompe con la conformidad constantemente y trata de enseñarle a Viggo como ser decente, mientras que este le enseña a él a soltarse. Es entretenida y el final te deja feliz.

sean porter’s crisp, polished cinematography paints a rich, nostalgic portrait of 1960s america, wrapping the journey in warm tones and elegant period framing that instantly signals prestige filmmaking. every frame is calculated for maximum audience accessibility, capturing the shifting American landscape from sleek urban nightscapes to vintage southern estates with smooth camera movements and flawless lighting. you can see exactly why this swept the academy awards, as the glossy visual finish combines effortlessly with a crowd-pleasing, classic narrative structure that hits every emotional beat with reliable precision. the plot functions as a classic study in defensive compartmentalisation and boundary breakdown between two completely contrasting personalities. don shirley guards his emotional vulnerability behind rigid posture, refined speech, and intellectual superiority to cope with the extreme isolation of being accepted by neither white elite circles nor his own community. conversely, tony lip relies on hyper-masculine bravado and unrefined pragmatism to mask his narrow worldview. as their physical journey south progresses, the forced proximity chips away at their respective psychological armour, forcing tony to confront his latent prejudices while don is pushed to strip away his loneliness and allow genuine human connection to break through his isolated facade.

Basicamente, assisti por estar baseado em uma história real. O filme retrata muitos anos atrás, em um país muito, muito racista. Grande parte das cenas me tirou a paciência, porque, apesar de eu não gostar de violência, quando não usamos sequer as palavras para nos defender, acabamos concordando com o que está acontecendo. Apesar de ser algo sobre o passado, algumas pequenas coisas ainda acontecem em 2026. Se você não concorda, não é negro ou vive em uma bolha... O racismo é cometido diariamente, mas, com toda certeza, avançamos muito! O filme é legal e vale a pena assistir, apesar de eu achar que poderia ser um pouco mais curto e, ainda assim, seria suficiente para retratar toda a história.

bon ça a un peu une vibez we are the world téléfilm 🫱🏻‍🫲🏿 mais à côté l’acting est bon, c’est assez bien réalisé et le scénario marche bien C’est dommage que le film n’est pas plus exploré les sujets raciales, l’homosexualité, la vie de Dr Shirley la dualité entre ne pas être assez noir pour les noirs et assez blanc pour les blancs, comment Tony a vécu le fait de ne pas vrmt être considéré comme blanc dans le sud…

“ it takes courage to change people’s hearts ” says the film without an ounce of courage. the acting is really good especially by viggo and overall its a pretty entertaining watch but the writing and story falls very flat. the film doesn’t take any risks and just culminates in an award-bait snooze fest with a shallow message made to make white people feel good about themselves.

It definitely suffers from the white savior trope, but it’s well-acted and has some witty moments. But I just keep thinking about how my friend said this movie feels like it was meant to be clipped and turned into YouTube shorts.

Watching this again, getting away from what I said about friendship, I got to think about this film from a different perspective. And it saldly made me enjoy it much less. This film is absurdly simplistic about racism, specially in that time, and it kinda falls into the white saviour clitché. The friendship is still there, and I was still smiling most of the film. But for the situation it's portraying, and the kind of journey it was, this film is way too comfortable to watch.

Amerikanize edilmiş modern zamanın Zorba'sı gibi hissettirdi. Irkçılık gibi toplumsal konuların yanında yalnızlık, yakın çevreye uyum sağlayamama, iki farklı karaktere sahip insanın tepkileri ve orta yolu bulma çabaları, dostluk gibi daha bireysel konular üzerinde düşündüren bir filmdi. Üstüne iki sevdiğim isim başrolde olunca film aktı gitti.

Likable leads hold a hoaky script above drowning-level. The ending ironically makes you feel like you ate too many Christmas cookies. Yes, you’re supposed to believe Doc Shirley doesn’t know who Aretha Franklin is or how to eat fried chicken. What do you mean a white guy directed the movie??

I’m very glad nothing bad happened (sometimes I don’t want my heart crushed), and Mahershala Ali is a very beautiful man. This is a pretty textbook explanation of race and identity, and I’m glad I live in a world where this story is no longer groundbreaking (I mean, to the communities I surround myself with). Makes me appreciate the work others have put in before me to make it feel this way. It was cute, and not what I had expected. With all the hype I had anticipated a more meaningful story—one that captured nuances and wasn’t so explicit with its messaging. But maybe what it is was exactly what it was meant to be.
